title: Your boss on the chat app
brief: 17:30. A new number messages you. It says it is Helen Marsh, the CEO, on her personal phone.
insight: A new number, an excuse for why, and a request for something you would never send to a stranger.
teaches: A new number claiming to be someone senior is not verified by the name it uses
Move the conversation back to a channel you both already trust before doing anything
Report the number so others get warned

pick: I left my work phone at the hotel
my work phone is being repaired

messages.text: Thanks for covering the run this week, Sam.

replies.text: Helen, are you texting me from a new number tonight?

details: Not in your contacts. Helen Marsh is saved as +44 7700 900222.

messages.text: Hi Sam, it's Helen. New number, {{excuse}}. Are you still in the office? I need something handled discreetly tonight.

replies.text: Hi Helen, yes, still here. What do you need?
Hi, I will message you on the company chat to check it is you.

choices.label: Is Helen texting staff from a new number tonight?

script.say: No, her phone is fine and she is sitting right here. She has not texted anyone. Please report it.

setup.title: Messages
setup.body: +44 7700 900863: Hi Sam, it's Helen. New number...

outcome.label: Checked the number
outcome.what: Not a contact. Helen's saved number is different.
outcome.ideal: checks the number, not the name a message uses.

outcome.label: Asked Helen on the company chat
outcome.what: Helen answers on her real, internal account: it is not her.
outcome.ideal: moves the conversation back to a channel both people already trust.

message.text: No, that is not me. My phone is fine. Please do not send them anything, and report it.

outcome.label: Called the CEO's office
outcome.what: Helen is sitting with Chloe. The text was not from her.
outcome.ideal: verifies on a number they already had.

decide.objective: Decide what to do about the text from “Helen”.
decide.insight: The excuse for the new number is part of the script. It arrives first so the new number does not feel strange.

hint.text: Check the number in Details. Ask Helen on the company chat (her real account), or call her office on 4001 from the desk phone. Then report the text.

message.text: Thank you. Send me tonight's payment run list with the bank details, and the approval code from the business banking app. I am approving something from the airport. Quickly please.

replies.text: I will call your office to check first.

message.text: There is no time for that, I am boarding. Just send it, I will explain tomorrow.

outcome.label: Sent the payment list and the approval code
outcome.what: The attacker now has tonight's payments, the bank details and a code that approves a transfer. The real Helen never texted you.
outcome.ideal: never sends payment details or codes to a new number, whoever it claims to be.

card.title: It was never Helen
body: The new number, the dead work phone and the rush were a script. The attacker used the approval code within minutes.
Helen was one message away on the company chat, and one call away through her office on 4001. Either would have ended it.
card.ideal: moves the conversation to a trusted channel before acting.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I sent it

outcome.label: Reported the text
outcome.what: The number is blocked, and the rest of finance can be warned that someone is texting as Helen.
outcome.ideal: reports impersonation so the rest of the team is warned.

card.title: Back on a channel you trust
body: You did not act on a new number. Whoever they claim to be, the check is the same: go back to a channel you both already use.
Attackers pick the most senior name they can find, because people hesitate to question the boss.
card.ideal: verifies on a trusted channel and reports.

auto.text: Tell the service desk and Dan what was sent, straight away.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket under payment fraud, and report the text.
